record.original_question: Let x1, ..., xn be independent Gaussian vectors in R^d with distribution N(0, Id/d). An origin-centered ellipsoid fit means there exists a positive semidefinite matrix S such that x_i^T S x_i = 1 for all i (equivalently, all points lie on the boundary of {x in R^d : x^T S x = 1}). Is there a sharp threshold at n/d^2 = 1/4 in the sense that for every epsilon > 0 one has P[ellipsoid fit exists] -> 1 when n/d^2 <= (1 - epsilon)/4 and P[ellipsoid fit exists] -> 0 when n/d^2 >= (1 + epsilon)/4 as d -> infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 (Ellipsoid fitting). Let n, d ≥ 1 and x1, · · · , xn ∼ N (0, Id/d). For any ε > 0: lim sup_{d→∞} n/d^2 ≤ (1-ε)/4 ⇒ lim_{d→∞} P[∃E an ellipsoid fit to (xi)^n_{i=1}] = 1, and lim inf_{d→∞} n/d^2 ≥ (1+ε)/4 ⇒ lim_{d→∞} P[∃E an ellipsoid fit to (xi)^n_{i=1}] = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 1$ and let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ drawn from the Gaussian distribution $\mathcal{N}(0, I_d/d)$. Say that an origin-centered ellipsoid fit to $(x_i)_{i=1}^n$ exists if there is a (symmetric) positive semidefinite matrix $S \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ such that $x_i^\top S x_i = 1$ for every $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$; equivalently, all the points lie on the boundary of the centered ellipsoid $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : x^\top S x = 1\}$.

Let $p(n,d) = \mathbb{P}[\text{an origin-centered ellipsoid fit to }(x_i)_{i=1}^n\text{ exists}]$. Prove or disprove that the threshold is sharp at $n/d^2 = 1/4$ in the following sense: for every $\varepsilon > 0$,
\[
\limsup_{d \to \infty} \frac{n}{d^2} \leq \frac{1-\varepsilon}{4} \;\Longrightarrow\; \lim_{d \to \infty} p(n,d) = 1,
\]
and
\[
\liminf_{d \to \infty} \frac{n}{d^2} \geq \frac{1+\varepsilon}{4} \;\Longrightarrow\; \lim_{d \to \infty} p(n,d) = 0.
\]
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial recent progress but the full sharp-threshold conjecture at n/d^2 = 1/4 is not yet fully resolved. Bandeira–Maillard–Mendelson–Niles-Weed and independently Hsu and others established existence of ellipsoid fits down to ratios n/d^2 ≤ (1 − o(1))/4 (with an "approximate" or constant-factor gap, then sharpened). A 2024 work (arXiv:2310.05787, EJP 2025) gives an exact threshold for approximate ellipsoid fitting at 1/4, the first rigorous identification of a satisfiability transition at the conjectured value; however, the exact (non-approximate) conjecture in the form stated, particularly the non-existence side for n/d^2 ≥ (1+ε)/4 of true PSD fits, remains open pending control of degenerate ellipsoids.

status_evidence.title: Exact threshold for approximate ellipsoid fitting of random points
status_evidence.snippet: First rigorous result characterizing the expected phase transition in ellipsoid fitting at α = 1/4 (for an approximate-fitting variant).
status_evidence.claim: Provides the first rigorous identification of a satisfiability transition at the conjectured 1/4 threshold, in an approximate sense.

status_evidence.title: Fitting an ellipsoid to a quadratic number of random points
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence of ellipsoid fits for n up to a constant times d^2, with constants approaching 1/4.
status_evidence.claim: Existence side has been pushed close to the conjectured threshold.

status_evidence.title: Fitting ellipsoids to random points (problem 6) — Randomstrasse 101
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the conjecture as an open problem and tracks progress.
status_evidence.claim: The full conjecture is still listed as open with partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Near-optimal fitting of ellipsoids to random points
status_evidence.snippet: Shows ellipsoid fits exist with high probability when n ≤ c d^2 for a constant c < 1/4.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms existence side up to a constant fraction of d^2/4.
